evidence: “The lounge window faces south and the sun falls on the freezer all afternoon.”
args.against: “The freezer door was open a crack with a box of paper plates stuck in it.”

d.note: Ten minutes is a short time and a whole morning is a long one, so this case can be argued with a clock. Cold air coming out into the room is the sentence that shows the door fault was still working at two. Ask which answer stops and which keeps going.

title: The Field Day Ribbon
story: On Field Day, Maya won a blue first-place ribbon. She clipped it to her water bottle and went to the sack race. When she came back, the ribbon was gone! A gust of wind blew everyone’s hats around. Maya saw something blue flapping against the fence at the edge of the field. It was her ribbon, caught on the wire. Her friend Ally had been in the sack race with her the whole time. The coach had all the extra ribbons locked in a box.

sus.why: gust of wind, ribbon caught on the fence
in the sack race with her the whole time
extra ribbons were locked in a box

ans: The wind blew Maya’s ribbon to the fence.
proof: "A gust of wind blew everyone’s hats around."
"It was her ribbon, caught on the wire."
clears: Ally: "Her friend Ally had been in the sack race with her the whole time."
Coach: "The coach had all the extra ribbons locked in a box."
explain: This shows the wind carried the ribbon because it ended up on the fence after a big gust. Because of this, nobody took it.

d.story: On Field Day, Maya won a blue first-place ribbon and clipped it to her water bottle. When she came back from the sack race it was gone. A gust of wind blew everyone's hats around. Something blue was flapping against the fence at the edge of the field. Ally finished the sack race early and went back for her bottle. The clip on Maya's ribbon was bent open before the race.
d.q: Where did the ribbon go? Pick one answer and prove it.

sus.why: a gust of wind and something blue on the fence
finished the sack race early and went back for her bottle
a clip already bent open before the race

evidence: “A gust of wind blew everyone's hats around.”
“Something blue was flapping against the fence at the edge of the field.”
args.against: “Ally finished the sack race early and went back for her bottle.”

evidence: “Ally finished the sack race early and went back for her bottle.”
args.against: “Something blue was flapping against the fence at the edge of the field.”

evidence: “The clip on Maya's ribbon was bent open before the race.”
args.against: “A gust of wind blew everyone's hats around.”

d.note: Something blue is not the same as the ribbon, and a careful reader will say so before anybody runs to the fence. The bent clip explains how the ribbon came off and says nothing about where it went. Two answers can both be needed, and that is worth naming.

title: The Popping Balloons
story: On the last day of school, the class tied balloons to the playground fence. One by one, they started to pop! The balloons were in the bright, hot sun, and the thermometer said 90 degrees. The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine. No one was near the fence, because everyone was eating popsicles under the tree. "The heat made the air inside get bigger!" said Ms. Jade.

sus.why: 90 degrees, sunny ones popped, shady ones were fine
everyone was under the tree
no clues point to birds

ans: The hot sun made the balloons pop.
proof: "The balloons were in the bright, hot sun, and the thermometer said 90 degrees."
"The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine."
clears: Students: "No one was near the fence, because everyone was eating popsicles under the tree."
explain: This shows the heat popped them because only the balloons in the sun popped. Because of this, the hot sun was the cause. (Science link: heat makes gas expand.)

d.story: On the last day of school the class tied balloons to the playground fence. One by one they started to pop. The balloons were in bright sun and the thermometer said ninety degrees. The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine. The fence has a line of sharp wire ends along the top rail. The sunny balloons were blown up biggest because they went up first.
d.q: Why did the balloons pop? Make the case for one answer.

sus.why: ninety degrees, with the shady ones still fine
a line of sharp wire ends along the top rail
blown up biggest because they went up first

evidence: “The balloons were in bright sun and the thermometer said ninety degrees.”
“The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine.”
args.against: “The fence has a line of sharp wire ends along the top rail.”

evidence: “The fence has a line of sharp wire ends along the top rail.”
args.against: “The balloons in the shade by the door were still fine.”

evidence: “The sunny balloons were blown up biggest because they went up first.”
args.against: “On the last day of school the class tied balloons to the playground fence.”

d.note: The shady balloons are the control and they are the best thing in the story, because they share the fence and not the sun. That beats the wire. The last sentence is the sly one: the sunny balloons were also the fullest, so sun and size travel together and the case cannot separate them.
